neighbours.label: An attributive adjective that names a physical or state property of the following noun (the soft tissues, the protected character, loss of firm-ness), vs the same phrases without the adjective
fire: Hard kibble can scrape the tender gums of an older cat.
The level ends when the shielded player loses all health.
Freezing caused a loss of crispness in the stored lettuce.
Rough handling can bruise the delicate skin of ripe peaches.
Wax will keep the weathered wood looking smooth for years.
The surgeon cut through the thick membrane around the joint.
Store the frozen samples in the coldest part of the freezer.
Dentists warn that sugar wears away the hard enamel of teeth.
quiet: Hard kibble can scrape the gums of an older cat.
The level ends when the player loses all health.
Freezing caused a loss of flavor in the stored lettuce.
Rough handling can bruise the peaches during transport.
Wax will keep the wood looking good for years.
The surgeon cut through the membrane around the joint.
Store the samples in the back of the freezer.
Dentists warn that sugar wears away the teeth over time.

predictions: Property adjectives reach 0.15-0.5; the same sentences without them stay under 0.05.
notes: Probe: soft 0.50, firm(ness) 0.49, protected 0.34, distressed 0.14, bright 0.14; adjective removed 0.008-0.03. Amplitude varies; median may fall near 0.2.
